sources.name: INAO — Délimitation des aires géographiques des SIQO
INAO — Délimitation parcellaire des AOC viticoles
IGN — BD TOPO®, vine zones (zone de végétation « Vigne »)
BRGM — Cartes géologiques harmonisées à 1/50 000 (BD Charm-50)
INRAE — Carte des sols de France (soil types, via IGN Géoplateforme)
Météo-France — SIM quotidienne (Safran-Isba reanalysis, 8 km grid)

truthBoundary: Appellation size is a count of communes, not a quality level: INAO publishes no level (cru, villages, regional) for this region. “Small” means the most specific appellation covering the place spans 1–7 communes within the region, “large” means 40 or more.
The vignobles follow a geographic grouping of appellations typed by hand (scripts/data/languedoc-subregions.json), not an official list; edges are approximate.
Vineyard land is the vine cover mapped by IGN in BD TOPO, not the INAO parcel delimitation. Check the Gard and Bouches-du-Rhône edges (Sable de Camargue) for gaps.

Appellation areas come from the INAO parcel delimitation (informational; the official plan is the one filed at the town hall or with INAO) cut to the mapped vines. Where an appellation shape and a lieu-dit are too complex for an exact intersection, their overlap is measured on a grid of points (typically within about one point of the place’s area).
Surface geology is the rock unit mapped at 1:50 000 under the plot, not the soil. Where the legend states no stage, age is inferred from the unit’s name, code or kind (marked ≈) or left blank.

Weather is the Météo-France SIM reanalysis (Safran-Isba, built from ground observations) for the surrounding 8 km grid cell, not a measurement on the plot. Its daily extremes come from hourly values: against 16 Météo-France stations it ran typically 0.5–2 °C below measured maximum temperatures, differed on minimum temperatures by up to about 2 °C either way, and missed hot days and local cold-air pockets. Daily rain and temperatures tracked the stations closely. GDD base 10 °C, evapotranspiration is Météo-France potential evapotranspiration, climate type from 1991–2020 monthly normals.
Soil type is the dominant type mapped by INRAE at regional scale where the plot lies, not a measurement on the plot.
